text: The authors prove (informally stated) that for a set family M, the population expansion c(U) cannot be much smaller than the empirical estimate c-hat(U) computed from finite samples of A and B with a neighborhood oracle: with probability at least 1 - delta, the supremum over U in M of c-hat(U) - c(U) is bounded by a term that hides constants and log factors and scales with the VC dimension of M over the sample size n_A.
title: Theorem 5.1: expansion can be checked statistically from finite samples
